security_problem: Round-8 Codex P2: both constructors call resolveLaunchedIdentity(cfg) BEFORE wirePolicyReload(). resolveLaunchedIdentity can stream the executable and declared entry payloads while the policy watcher is already running; until wirePolicyReload() installs the atomic commitPolicyRuntime transaction, a watcher reload that publishes during identity hashing publishes the new policy directly. That can produce a mixed-generation runtime: engine.Policy() = generation B while the redactor, audit redaction patterns, and approval timeout stay generation A. PR #60 introduces potentially slow identity hashing before reload wiring and materially enlarges the exploitable race window.
required_behavior: wirePolicyReload() installs the atomic reload transaction BEFORE resolveLaunchedIdentity(cfg) in BOTH New and NewWithTracing, so once potentially slow invocation hashing starts, every watcher reload goes through commitPolicyRuntime(...) and publishes policy+redactor+audit patterns+approval timeout atomically under runtimeMu. Startup identity remains single-snapshot coherent: resolveLaunchedIdentity captures exactly ONE policy pointer and uses that same snapshot for identity measurement and attestation shape; a reload during identity hashing never relabels a digest measured under generation A with generation B's shape. Identity stays immutable: commitPolicyRuntime never re-resolves or re-installs server identity. A deterministic blocked-resolver regression test proves the transaction is installed before hashing: policy A current, constructor begins, reload transaction installed, resolver blocks, watcher publishes B, resolver unblocks, constructor completes; engine policy == B, redactor corresponds to B, approval timeout corresponds to B, audit redaction patterns correspond to B; launch identity + launch shape stay coherently derived from the ONE snapshot A; if B changes the attestation contract, tools/call fails closed with a restart-required deny rather than incorrectly attested.
failure_behavior: Fail closed for tools/call when a watcher reload during identity hashing produces mixed-generation runtime surfaces; never report server_attested=true for a contract never measured; never leak call arguments on an identity-gate deny.
